UPSTREAM: arch/x86: Implement minimal bootblock for C_ENVIRONMENT_BOTOBLOCK Some newer x86 systems can boot from non-memory-mapped boot media (e.g. EMMC). The bootblock may be backed by small amounts of SRAM, or other memory, similar to how most ARM chipsets work. In such cases, we may not have enough code space for romstage very early on. This means that CAR setup and early boot media (e.g. SPI, EMMC) drivers need to be implemented within the limited amount memory of storage available. Since the reset vector has to be contained in this early code memory, the bootblock is the best place to implement loading of other stages. Implement a bootblock which does the minimal initialization, up to, and including switch to protected mode. This then transfers control to platform-specific code. No stack is needed, and control is transferred via a "jmp" such that no stack operations are involved. CHROMIUM: mac80211: mesh path selection stability enhancements To increase path selection stability, we want to favor the same nexthop and only switch when the alternative is considerablly better than the current one. The new logic is as follows: 0. throw away updates from past epochs 1. always update info if the nexthop is the same, because - We want to get latest link metric for the chosen nexthop - This will update lifetime of the path so we can keep using the same nexthop 2. if update is for a different nexthop, update if the new link metric is path_switch_threshold % better. - path_switch_threshold is tunable from debugfs Note that the existing implementation will always update if it sees a new epoch, but here we want to wait for updates for the same nexthop. This may cause the path to expire if we don't see the same nexthop update in time. This can be helped by doubling the path lifetime (currently 6s) so we can afford to lose 1 update for the same nexthop. CHROMIUM: mac80211: send packets to mesh peers without routing Mesh links that are not picked by HWMP will not be exercised and therefore we can't get link quality updates from such links. To exercise these links we need a way to bypass mesh routing, but only for the data packets we inject, not for normal packets. The assumption is that the injected packets will have DA = all 0s and SA = mesh peer MAC. The reason is that mac80211 mesh code is only interested in DA and by putting 0 pattern in DA we can eliminate extra logic for normal packets. In the exception case, if we see 0s then correct the addrs, put the mesh peer in RA/DA/meshDA and bypass HWMP. There is a compile flag to turn on/off this. Add caviat to handle corrupted FW for Melfas Melfas touchscreens will suffer from a corrupted FW when power is pulled during a FW update. On the next boot, the touchscreen will report it's product ID as "T4H0_BOOTLOADER" instead of whatever the real product ID is. Previously, the updater script would have seen that it doesn't match the product ID associated with the FW binary on disk, and aborted the update. This CL ads in a caviat, so if the updater script can detect that the FW was corrupted, it should continue anyway. The Meflas driver simply pulls a FW from a static filename as well, so as long as the updater script doesn't abort, the update will recover the touchscreen. As a result of this deficiency, Melfas touchscreens can never be dual-sourced. Since we can lose the product ID, we lose the ability to differentiate two Melfas touchscreens reliably. BUG=chrome-os-partner:52653 TEST=deployed onto a Reks with a Melfas TS and tested by corrupting the TS FW and watching the script recover it automatically after a reboot.
